# Results — Study 558 (Failures-To-Deliver): do settlement-fail spikes foreshadow a squeeze?

*Generated by [`failures_to_deliver/compute.py`](../failures_to_deliver/compute.py), fully offline
and deterministic. There is **no free FTD tape** (the SEC fails-to-deliver file is a bulk,
semi-monthly, CUSIP-keyed flat file with no price panel and no retail endpoint — see
[`data.py`](../failures_to_deliver/data.py) and [`docs/references.md`](references.md)), so this
study is **synthetic-only** and the reproducible headline is the deterministic **seed-558 null
world** (folklore off): with FTD spikes carrying no forward information, does the honest
event-study engine correctly report **nothing**? Panel fingerprint `c0ab49b6db5b` (60 names × 756
days). As-of **2026-06-30**.*

## The verdict, earned — Signal `NONE` · Tradability `MIRAGE` · "Squeeze predictor?" `BUSTED`

Meme-stock-era microstructure folklore: a **spike in failures-to-deliver** (settlement fails)
means shorts are trapped, so a **short squeeze** is imminent and the **forward return after an FTD
spike is large and positive**. We test that as a market-adjusted **event study** on a faithful
synthetic FTD panel.

On the reproducible **null world** (FTD spikes carry no forward information — the honest baseline),
the post-spike **abnormal** forward return is **−0.03%** over the 5-day horizon (one-sample *t* on
market-adjusted abnormal returns = **−0.14**), and the **label-shuffle placebo *p* = 0.513** sits
dead-centre — spike labels carry no forward information, exactly as planted. So `NONE` on the
signal axis. The engine is **not** blind: the synthetic positive control (below) shows that when a
real post-spike pop *is* planted, the seed-robust abnormal-*t* climbs straight past +2 — so the
flat null is a true negative, not a dead detector.

Because there is **no free real FTD tape**, this study cannot clear the `REAL` bar (which needs a
robust *t* ≥ 2 on a real tape) — the ceiling is `WEAK`/`NONE`, and the honest run lands at `NONE`.

## The event study — the null world says NOTHING

Flag FTD-spike events (trailing z-score ≥ 2.5, causal), take the forward 5-day cumulative return,
and **market-adjust** (subtract the cross-name forward return that day) to isolate the *abnormal*
post-spike pop. A refractory period keeps events non-overlapping so the *t* is honest.

| | value |
|---|---|
| Spike events (refractory-thinned, 60 names × 756 days) | **829** |
| Raw post-spike forward return (5d) | +0.15% |
| Market baseline forward return (5d) | +0.18% |
| **Abnormal post-spike return** (market-adjusted) | **−0.03%** |
| **One-sample *t* on abnormal returns** | **−0.14** |
| Label-shuffle placebo *p* (1000 perms) | **0.513** |

The abnormal post-spike return is essentially zero (slightly negative), the *t* is **−0.14**, and
the placebo *p* is a coin-flip **0.513**. The folklore's promised pop is absent by construction and
the honest engine reports absence.

## Robustness sweep — and the multiple-comparisons trap it exposes

Re-run across forward horizons {1, 3, 5, 10 days} × spike thresholds {2.0, 2.5, 3.0} — **on the
same null world** (where, by construction, there is nothing):

| horizon | spike_z | n events | abnormal % | *t* |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1 | 2.0 | 1871 | −0.14% | **−2.23** |
| 1 | 2.5 | 1382 | −0.16% | **−2.23** |
| 1 | 3.0 | 1053 | −0.16% | −1.87 |
| 3 | 2.0 | 1222 | −0.21% | −1.53 |
| 3 | 2.5 | 948 | −0.08% | −0.56 |
| 3 | 3.0 | 764 | −0.04% | −0.24 |
| 5 | 2.0 | 1009 | −0.20% | −1.00 |
| 5 | 2.5 | 829 | −0.03% | −0.14 |
| 5 | 3.0 | 694 | −0.01% | −0.03 |
| 10 | 2.0 | 812 | −0.17% | −0.54 |
| 10 | 2.5 | 700 | +0.23% | +0.67 |
| 10 | 3.0 | 606 | +0.22% | +0.62 |

The sweep *t* ranges **−2.23 → +0.67**. Note the honesty lesson: on a **pure-noise** panel,
cherry-picking the 1-day horizon manufactures a |*t*| > 2 (the *wrong* sign, at that). A signal you
have to hunt for across a grid of horizons and thresholds is a multiple-comparisons artifact, not a
squeeze predictor — the classic data-mined-significance trap.

## Null across 30 seeds — the folklore looks "real" on some cuts by luck

Run the headline event study (h = 5, z = 2.5) on 30 independent null worlds (seeds 558–587):

| | value |
|---|---|
| Mean abnormal *t* across 30 seeds | **+0.20** |
| SD of abnormal *t* | **1.12** |
| Fraction of seeds with \|*t*\| > 2 | **6.7%** |

Averaged over seeds the *t* is ≈ 0 (no signal), with a spread close to a standard normal — so
about 1 seed in 15 *individually* prints a |*t*| > 2 with no effect present. That is precisely why
a single striking post-FTD-spike chart proves nothing.

## Costs

| | value |
|---|---|
| Gross abnormal post-spike return (null, 5d) | −0.03% |
| Net (5 bps/leg round-trip + 300 bps/yr borrow, 5-day hold) | **−0.19%** |

FTD-spiking names are exactly the expensive, hard-to-borrow tail, so the borrow (charged as if the
long were paired against / financed by a short in the same name) is deliberately punitive. There is
nothing to harvest before costs, and costs make it worse — `MIRAGE`.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is faithful (seed-robust, 25 seeds)

Plant a *real* post-spike pop (``squeeze_alpha`` = extra forward drift on post-spike days) of
increasing strength and average the abnormal-*t* over 25 seeds (house rule, ≥ 20 seeds):

| Planted `squeeze_alpha` | Mean abnormal *t* (25 seeds) | reads as |
|--:|--:|---|
| 0.000 (null) | **+0.14** | flat — no false signal |
| 0.002 | +1.78 | pop emerging |
| 0.004 | +3.42 | clears the bar |
| 0.006 | +5.05 | pop visible |
| 0.010 | +8.26 | strong |

At the null the abnormal-*t* is ≈ 0; planting a genuine post-spike pop drives it straight past +2
as it grows. As a single-world illustration, planting `squeeze_alpha = 0.006` (seed 558) yields an
abnormal post-spike return of **+1.05%** at *t* **+4.92**, placebo *p* **0.001**. The detector
works — so the flat null is a **true negative**, not a broken engine.

## Honesty checks

- **Execution lag.** A spike is identified from the FTD level at day t (public, if lagged, in the
  real world); the position is entered at day t's close and the forward return is measured over
  **t+1 .. t+5**. The signal never sees a future return (no look-ahead). The one-bar entry lag is
  the single documented convention.
- **Non-overlapping events.** FTD is persistent (spikes cluster), so raw event windows overlap and
  the returns are dependent; a refractory period (one horizon) makes kept events disjoint so the
  *t* is not inflated by pseudo-replication.
- **Costs one-way × NAV, shorts pay borrow.** Round-trip cost on the long leg plus a punitive
  annual borrow on the FTD-spiking name (the trapped-shorts story is *about* shorts, and these are
  the hard-to-borrow tail).
- **Data availability, on the Signal axis.** There is no free FTD tape; the study is synthetic-only
  and therefore *cannot* earn `REAL` (which needs a robust *t* ≥ 2 on a real tape). Every synthetic
  cell is labelled as such and never sits under a real-tape banner.

## The honest takeaway

Failures-to-deliver spikes as a short-squeeze predictor are microstructure **folklore**. The
academic literature (Boni 2006; Evans et al. 2009; Fotak et al. 2014) says fails are mostly
settlement plumbing and cost-of-borrow, not cornered shorts — if anything associated with *better*
liquidity and *lower* volatility. We cannot run it on a real tape (no free FTD data), so we do the
honest thing: build a faithful synthetic event-study engine, prove it detects a *planted* squeeze,
and show that with **no** planted effect it correctly finds **nothing** — abnormal post-spike return
−0.03%, *t* −0.14, placebo *p* 0.513 — while a horizon/threshold sweep manufactures a spurious
|*t*| > 2 on pure noise. `NONE` × `MIRAGE`, squeeze-predictor claim `BUSTED`.
